market_name: Will 9 Fed rate cuts happen in 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the market's move coincides with a fresh macro headline (weak jobs data, financial stress) versus thin-liquidity noise; confirm Treasury futures are moving.
time_plan.1h: Compare TLT tick against 2y/10y yield changes and Fed funds futures repricing to see if bonds are actually rallying.
time_plan.2h: Assess whether move persists or mean-reverts; watch equity risk sentiment for corroborating recession signal.
time_plan.6h: Re-evaluate against any Fed speaker commentary or economic releases; check if curve is bull-steepening (recession) vs bull-flattening.
time_plan.12h: Close-of-window review: did TLT hold gains, and did the prediction-market probability sustain its move or fade?

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of 9 Fed cuts in 2026 (225bps of easing) reflects expectations of severe economic deterioration or emergency easing. Aggressive dovish repricing pulls the front-end and belly of the curve lower and, in a growth-scare scenario, drives a flight to duration, lifting long-Treasury prices. TLT is a liquid, direct proxy for falling long-end yields.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Confirm whether real yields and DXY are moving consistently with a dovish repricing.
time_plan.1h: Check gold futures vs dollar index correlation to validate the driver is rate expectations.
time_plan.2h: Watch for mean reversion; distinguish safe-haven bid from pure rate story.
time_plan.6h: Reassess against any macro data or Fed commentary shifting cut expectations.
time_plan.12h: End-of-window check: did GLD hold, and did the market probability remain elevated?

predictions.reasoning: An extreme-dovish scenario (9 cuts) implies lower real rates and a weaker dollar, both supportive for gold. Elevated odds also often accompany crisis/safe-haven demand, reinforcing the direction. GLD is a liquid proxy.

evidence_used: Market question targets 9 cuts (225bps) in 2026, an extreme-dovish/crisis-consistent outcome
Rate-cut expectations map directly to Treasury yields, gold, and the dollar
12h window and 700bps tradable threshold are demanding for macro ETFs
uncertainty_notes: A move in a low-probability tail market is very noisy and often thin-liquidity driven
Direction is ambiguous: 'controlled easing into soft landing' vs 'crisis emergency cuts' imply different equity/credit reactions even if bonds rally
Expected 12h magnitudes are well below the 700bps tradable threshold, so this is not a tradable signal

llm_justification.summary: The market asks whether the Fed delivers 9 cuts (225bps) in 2026 — a deeply dovish, recession/crisis-consistent scenario. A sharp rise in its implied probability would signal expectations of aggressive easing, which most cleanly maps to lower long-end yields (TLT up) and higher gold (GLD up) via lower real rates and a softer dollar. Both mappings are modest-confidence and, importantly, expected 12h moves fall far short of the 700bps tradable bar, so this is research-only.
key_assumptions: A probability spike reflects genuine dovish/macro information rather than market microstructure noise
The dovish signal transmits to rates and gold within a 12h window
No offsetting hawkish surprise or already-public information dominates
failure_modes: The probability move is noise in an illiquid tail market and reverses quickly
Information is already public (data already released), so assets have already repriced
A 'soft-landing' interpretation lifts equities and dampens the safe-haven bid, muddying gold/bond directions
TLT/GLD are only indirectly exposed and could be dominated by unrelated flows
Move magnitude far below the 700bps threshold means no actionable edge
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
